# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a stout, fat woman who waddles when she walks.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P19](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0019), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable, industrious, and notable housewife who manages her own affairs and her neighbors' with equal vigour. She is remarkably inquisitive, outspoken, and proud of always speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly opinionated and prone to pessimism, she loves to create a sensation and prided herself on her active involvement in church and community work. Despite her sharp tongue, she possesses a kindly heart at core.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P30](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0030), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road of Avonlea, keeping a sharp eye on all passers-by. Upon seeing Matthew Cuthbert unusually dressed up and driving out of Avonlea, her curiosity led her to visit Green Gables, where Marilla Cuthbert informed her of their intention to adopt an orphan boy. Mrs. Rachel voiced strong disapproval and pessimism regarding the decision, and later spread the news through the community. Weeks later, after recovering from a severe bout of grippe, she visited Green Gables to inspect the adopted orphan, Anne Shirley, but offended the child by calling her skinny, homely, freckled, and red-headed, provoking an angry outburst from Anne. Though initially indignant and advising a whipping, Mrs. Rachel readily accepted Anne's dramatic apology the following evening, forgave her, and offered her a bouquet of June lilies. Subsequently, Mrs. Rachel interacted frequently with the Cuthbert household, keeping track of Anne's doings at school and Sunday-school.

## Quotes

> I’ll just step over to Green Gables after tea and find out from Marilla where he’s gone and why.  <sub>[v1 c1 P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005)</sub>

> Well, Marilla, I’ll just tell you plain that I think you’re doing a mighty foolish thing—a risky thing, that’s what.  <sub>[v1 c1 P25](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0025)</sub>

> She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say.  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

> There, there, get up, child. Of course I forgive you. I guess I was a little too hard on you, anyway. But I’m such an outspoken person. You just mustn’t mind me, that’s what.  <sub>[v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034)</sub>

> Preserve me from a sly child, that’s what. On the whole, Marilla, I kind of like her.  <sub>[v1 c10 P38](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0038)</sub>
